distinguishing_features: Passive localized field-grading pad rather than predictive monitoring or tripping
Low-effective-permittivity porous epoxy with engineered void fraction and cavity size
Placement at FEM-identified barrier-interface electric-field hotspots
Purported reduction of local transient field during fast-rising voltage spikes without added sensors or insulation thickness
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce the peak electric field at winding-insulation defects below the partial-discharge inception threshold during steep voltage transients without increasing insulation thickness, thermal mass, or relying on active monitoring.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated field-reduction relation is physically reversed for series dielectric layers: continuity of normal displacement makes a lower-permittivity pad carry a higher electric field, shifting or concentrating the stress at its voids and interfaces rather than demonstrating the claimed reduction.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Although the closest art only monitors insulation degradation, the proposed localized voided low-permittivity pad and its claimed spike-specific field shaping would require non-routine material and interface design rather than an obvious monitoring-based modification.
